question: I have a mental health condition — does that mean I'm more likely to smoke?
answer: Yes, individuals with behavioral health conditions are more likely to smoke, accounting for 38% of all U.S. adult cigarette consumption, despite making up only 25% of the population. This group has a smoking rate of 23%, which is higher than the general adult rate of 14%.
